title: Processing Human Thymic Tissue for Single Cell RNA-Seq
protocol: Decontaminate working spaces and equipment with UV light and 70% ethyl alcohol before beginning thymus dissection.
Place the thymus into a petri dish containing 10 mL DPBS.
Add 10 mL of D10 at room temperature (20°C–22°C) to a 50 mL centrifuge tube with a cell strainer on top.
Slice the thymus using tweezers and a scalpel while it is in the petri dish.
Cut the thymus into 1 cm chunks and place them into a cell strainer in a petri dish.
Mash the thymus chunks using the flat end of a 5 mL syringe piston (without the piston) to filter cells into the petri dish, creating a cell suspension in DPBS.
Pipette the cell suspension from the petri dish through the cell strainer into a 50 mL centrifuge tube to further remove clumps.
Break or cut the tip of the pipette to increase bore size if clumping occurs and clogs the pipette.
Add additional DPBS to the petri dish and continue mashing chunks until no more cells are released.
Transfer the final cell suspension to the 50 mL tube.
Maintain Ficoll at 20°C–22°C (room temperature) to maintain ideal density for separation of layers.
Count the cells using a method that excludes RBCs (pre-Ficoll cell count).
Reconstitute RBCs in a 10 μL aliquot with 3% acetic acid at a dilution ratio of 1:500 to 1:1000 for counting on a hemocytometer.
Dilute the cell suspension to achieve a concentration of 20 million cells/mL using DPBS.
Calculate the number of cells needed for the experiment based on requirements.
Calculate the number of 50 mL centrifuge tubes required for processing the sample.
Add 15 mL Ficoll to each prepared tube before adding cells.
Mix diluted cell suspension thoroughly by pipetting to ensure even concentration.
Slowly layer 30 mL of the cell suspension onto the Ficoll in each tube, ensuring minimal mixing.
Keep the Ficoll tubes with cells at 20°C–22°C (room temperature).
Centrifuge all tubes at 400 × g for 30 minutes at 20°C–22°C without brake (Decel=Off).
Aspirate and discard the upper layer containing plasma, leaving 10–15 mL of plasma above the mononuclear cell layer.
Collect the buffy layer containing the mononuclear cells.
Transfer the collected buffy layer to a new 50 mL centrifuge tube.
Repeat the process with each additional tube, transferring each buffy layer of cells to a separate, new tube.
Transfer the buffy layer from each tube to a separate new tube.
Bring each tube up to 50 mL with DPBS.
Centrifuge at 300 × g for 10 minutes at 4°C using low brake.
Transfer the supernatant to a new container and combine all supernatants into one container on ice.
Add 10 mL of Miltenyi Buffer to one tube containing a cell pellet.
Resuspend the pellet in this buffer by mixing well.
Transfer the 10 mL of re-suspended cells to the next tube containing a cell pellet.
Resuspend the cell pellet in tube 2 with these 10 mL.
Continue transferring and resuspending the cells from each tube until all pellets are combined into one tube using Miltenyi Buffer.
Add an additional 10 mL Miltenyi Buffer to the first tube and transfer similarly to steps 22–24 to recover any remaining cells.
Count the recovered cells using a method that excludes RBCs (post-Ficoll cell count).
Re-suspend the cells in 300 μL of Miltenyi Buffer for every 400 million cells.
Add 100 μL of FCR blocking reagent and 100 μL of Anti-CD34 (Anti-Hapten) Microbeads for every 400 million cells.
Mix by gently tapping the tube.
Incubate the cells in a refrigerator for 30 min.
Remove the cells from the refrigerator and bring up to 50 mL with Miltenyi Buffer.
Centrifuge the cells (300 × g, 10 min, 4°C, Low Brake).
Attach the magnet to the magnetic stand in the biosafety cabinet.
Place the LS column in the magnet holder.
Place a pre-separation filter in the LS column.
Collect CD34– cells under the column in a 50 mL tube from the flow through of the column.
Equilibrate the column by pipetting 3 ml Miltenyi Buffer into the pre-separation filter.
Remove the supernatant and re-suspend cells in 5 ml Miltenyi Buffer.
Add the re-suspended cells to the pre-separation filter/column.
Rinse the centrifuge tube with 3 ml Miltenyi Buffer to recover remaining cells.
Wait for the first 5 ml of cells to completely pass through the column before adding the next 3 ml of rinsed cells to the pre-separation filter/column.
Wash the pre-separation filter/column six times with 3 ml Miltenyi Buffer.
Wait until the previous wash has completely filtered through before adding a new wash.
Perform 5-6 washes for maximum purity using Miltenyi Buffer.
Remove excess buffer from the column if it stops flowing and continue with step 39.
Place the magnetic column over a new 15 ml conical tube after the last wash is completed.
Add 5 ml of Miltenyi Buffer into the column after placing it in a new conical tube.
Insert the plunger into the column and push hard to extract CD34+ cells from the beads.
Perform a viable cell count for CD34– cells on ice.
Perform a viable cell count for CD34+ cells using trypan blue and hemocytometer or an automated cell counter.
Proceed immediately with FACS for isolation of highly enriched populations of viable CD34+ or CD34– cells for single cell RNA-seq.
Cryopreserve CD34+ cells if further isolation is to be performed at a later time.
Sort CD34– thymic cells predominantly consisting of double positive (DP) cells using FACS.
Use fresh CD34– cells rather than cryopreserved ones for maximizing viability in single cell RNA-seq.
Separate 20 million CD34– cells.
Separate 20,000 CD34+ cells (unstained control).
Centrifuge the CD34+ and CD34– cell suspensions at 300 × g for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Aspirate the supernatant to a volume of 40 μL buffer per 20 million CD34– cells.
Aspirate the supernatant to a volume of 20 μL buffer per 2.5 million CD34+ cells.
Block cryopreserved CD34+ cells in 40 μL blocking buffer for 5 min on ice.
Add FCR blocking reagent when processing cells for MACS if using fresh cells directly after MACS.
Add the appropriate antibody mix to the cells and incubate for 15 min at 4°C.
Add 3 mL PBS + 1% FBS to each tube containing antibody-stained cells.
Strain the cell suspension into a new Filter FACS tube.
Centrifuge the cell suspension (300 × g, 4°C, 5 min).
Bring down volume of supernatant to achieve concentration of roughly 5 million - 10 million cells/mL.
Add 2.5 μL sterile DAPI to stained cells a few minutes prior to starting FACS.
Sort desired populations into 100% FBS in sterile, capped tubes and transfer onto ice.
Use a 70 μm nozzle to minimize sort time and dilution of the FBS in the collection tube from sheath fluid volume carry over.
Run cells on the flow cytometer at a rate of 500–3,000 events/s during FACS.
Invert collection tubes coated with FBS to remove air bubbles and place on ice prior to sorting.
Sort cells into 300 μl of 100% FBS in a 1.5 ml Eppendorf tube for up to 5 × 10^5 cells or use a 5 ml FACS tube with 1 ml FBS for higher cell numbers.
Mix each collection tube by inversion after sorting to suspend the cells in FBS.
Sort 400,000 CD34+Lin– cells into a 1.5 ml Eppendorf tube and 1 million CD34–CD45+GlyA– cells into a FACS tube.
Sort an additional 10,000 CD34+CD7–CD1a– cells into the same collection tube containing 400,000 CD34+Lin– cells.
Transfer the sorted cells to a 15 mL conical tube.
Rinse out any leftover cells in the original collection tube with additional Miltenyi Buffer and transfer to the 15 mL conical tube.
Bring the volume up to 15 mL with Miltenyi Buffer.
Centrifuge at 300 × g for 5 minutes at 4°C using a standard brake.
Aspirate the supernatant, leaving behind approximately 40 μL of liquid.
Bring the volume up to 4 mL with D10 medium.
Remove the filter cap from a Filter FACS Tube and hold it over a 15 mL conical tube.
Filter the cell suspension into the 15 mL conical tube.
Centrifuge at 300 × g for 5 minutes at 4°C using a standard brake.
Aspirate the supernatant down to a volume of 50–80 μL.
Re-suspend the cell pellet with a P20 or P200 micropipette to avoid cell loss.
Count cells using a cell counter and a hemocytometer.
Proceed with single cell RNA-seq library preparation.
Adjust cell counter settings for CD34– and CD34+ human thymic cells prior to use.
Use a hemocytometer count in parallel with the electronic cell counter results.
Cryopreserve isolated cells as an optional step (timing: 10 min).
Centrifuge cells at 300 × g for 5 minutes at 4°C using standard brake.
Remove supernatant from the cells without disturbing them.
Add FBS + 10% DMSO to cells to reach a volume of 1 mL per tube and resuspend cells.
Aliquot cells into cryovials.
Transfer cryovials into a freezing container.
Place the freezing container in -80°C freezer immediately after adding FBS + 10% DMSO.
After 24-48 hours, transfer vials from the freezing container to a liquid nitrogen freezer.
Warm D10 medium to room temperature by leaving it in a low-light area or using a heated water bath for 5-10 minutes.
Remove the cryovial containing 1 mL of frozen cells from the liquid nitrogen freezer.
Place the vial immediately into a 37°C water bath.
Gently swirl the vial until just a tiny sliver of ice remains (1–2 min).
Spray the outside of the vial with 70% ethanol.
Transfer the vial into the biosafety cabinet to prevent contamination.
Transfer the cells to a 15 mL conical tube.
Slowly add room temperature D10 dropwise into the tube containing the thawed cells to bring the volume up to 15 mL.
Shake the tube while adding D10.
Centrifuge cell samples at 300 × g, 5 min, at room temperature (20°C–22°C).
Aspirate as much of the supernatant as possible without disturbing the cell pellet to remove as much DMSO as possible.
Gently re-suspend the cells in appropriate media or buffer for downstream studies.
